about.title: La Mesa Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: La Mesa's mix of freeway traffic and busy local streets means collisions happen where I-8 meets SR-125, along Fletcher Parkway, and across University Avenue. Public records show 320 injury collisions and 446 injured people in the most recent year, with reports clustering on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. as commuters and weekend traffic overlap. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days afterward matter: insurance adjusters move quickly, evidence can disappear, and California's rules on shared fault mean how the story gets told affects your claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured people in La Mesa with independent personal injury attorneys who handle these cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Our goal is to make that first step easier during an already stressful time.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but claims against a government entity (like a city-maintained road) can require notice in as little as six months.

items.title: Shared Fault Won't Necessarily Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible, you may still recover damages reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in standard car accident cases, which is one reason how your claim is documented matters.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements, made while you're still processing what happened, to minimize what they owe. An independent attorney can advise you on what to share and when.

items.question: What if my accident happened at the I-8 and SR-125 interchange or another busy La Mesa corridor?
items.answer: Crashes at high-traffic points like the I-8/SR-125 interchange, Fletcher Parkway, or University Avenue often involve multiple parties and layered evidence, including traffic camera footage or CHP reports. An attorney can help identify and preserve that evidence before it's lost or overwritten.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive's connection service is free, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
